name: "The Rock" Drake Erich
caption: Lost HOWF's opening match of its own opening broadcast to "Ultra Rocker" James Cortez by backslide.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

name: "Ultra Rocker" James Cortez
caption: Won the very first match in HOWF history, pinning "The Rock" Drake Erich with a backslide in just over two minutes.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

name: Fast Fighter
caption: Won HOWF's second-ever match against the self-declared deity Cyric, the Dark Sun, busting him open and finishing him with a hockey stick.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

name: Cyric, the Dark Sun
caption: A self-declared god with a ringside cult of followers, lost HOWF's second-ever match to Fast Fighter after his opponent used a hockey stick as a weapon.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

name: Ace Goodheart
caption: Lost to The Mosher in just over two minutes on HOWF's opening broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

name: The Mosher
caption: Beat Ace Goodheart with a power bomb on HOWF's opening broadcast; billed by the broadcast team as soon to hold titles in two other UEA-alliance feds.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

name: "Marauder" Mark Price
caption: Made Hiro Ozaka submit to the STF on HOWF's opening broadcast, with his manager Shannon and bodyguard Sentinel at ringside.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

name: Hiro Ozaka
caption: Lost to "Marauder" Mark Price by submission on HOWF's opening broadcast after a hard-fought thirteen-minute match.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

name: Big Jim Sphinks
caption: Won HOWF's opening triangle match, pinning Mike Higgins with a power bomb while Outcast Rob Cole looked on.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

name: Mike Higgins
caption: Pinned by Big Jim Sphinks in HOWF's opening triangle match, also involving Outcast Rob Cole.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

name: "Outcast" Rob Cole
caption: Wrestled in HOWF's opening triangle match, won by Big Jim Sphinks over tag partner Mike Higgins.

tenures.source: The fed's own first broadcast (Thursday Night Meltdown, 22 August 1996).

identity.note: Shares a name with the RSPWF Top 200's own "Outcast" Rob Cole (tagged AWMC/AGW, 1999-2000) across the tree — a generic ring-gimmick name reused independently by many unrelated feds across different eras; no shared operator, roster, host, or crossover document found. A bare name match is not evidence of a join under the identity-join test, so this stays distinct pending any actual corroboration. Also shares a first name only with the unrelated, later IHWF gimmick "Outcast" (2001).
